extracted.intended_audience: claimants, respondents, and their counsel participating in Copyright Claims Board proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive standards governing protective orders, evidence, discovery (interrogatories, document requests, additional discovery, expert testimony, requests for admission, sanctions), and smaller-claims practice before the Copyright Claims Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard protective order - standard of use
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery material received from another party may be used only in connection with the proceeding, and all copies must be returned or disposed of within 30 days of a determination or dismissal, or within 30 days of the exhaustion of the time for any review or appeal of the Board's final determination, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for a standard protective order follow the procedures in §220.5(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality designation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery material may be designated as 'confidential' only if the party reasonably and in good faith believes that it consists of: (i) bona fide confidential financial information previously not disclosed to the public; (ii) bona fide confidential and non-obvious business plans, product development information, or advertising or marketing plans previously not disclosed to the public; (iii) any information of a truly personal or intimate nature regarding any individual not known by the public; or (iv) any other category of information that the Board grants leave to designate as 'confidential.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations must be made in good faith and fit within these categories; the Board may grant other categories on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: No blanket confidentiality designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must make confidentiality determinations on a document-by-document basis and shall not designate as 'confidential' all discovery material produced in bulk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Party-level or production-wide blanket markings are prohibited; each document requires individual consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting confidential information (seal or redact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential discovery materials, or references to or discussions of confidential discovery materials in other documents, may be submitted to the Board by either filing them under seal or redacting the confidential document. If filed under seal, the confidential document must be accompanied by a redacted copy that may be included in the public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Board's sealing procedures and include a public redacted version when filing under seal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board determination of confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice and an opportunity for the designating party to respond, the Board in its discretion may remove a confidentiality designation from any material on its own initiative or upon consideration of a request from a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must attempt to resolve disputes over confidentiality designations before bringing such disputes to the Board; requests to remove a designation follow §220.5(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom protective orders disfavored
rubrics_metrics.description: Custom protective orders negotiated by the parties are disfavored. The parties may request that the Board enter a custom protective order that has been negotiated by the parties and that may provide for additional protections for highly sensitive materials, but such a request must be accompanied by a stipulation explaining the need and must attach the custom order as an exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board has discretion to grant or deny such requests; follow §220.5(a)(1) procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction of personally identifiable information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of whether discovery material has been designated as 'confidential,' parties must redact social security numbers, taxpayer identification numbers, birth dates, health information protected by law, the names of any individuals known to be minors, and financial account numbers from any public filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This redaction requirement applies to all public filings to protect PII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations of protective order may be bad faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of a protective order may constitute bad-faith conduct pursuant to §232.3 of this subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper disclosures or misuse of protected material can trigger sanctions or other sanctions-related consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and weight of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: All evidence that is relevant and not unduly repetitious or privileged shall be admissible. Evidence which has authentication or credibility issues will have its weight discounted accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may discount or exclude evidence with serious credibility issues, or request clarification from a party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness examination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: All witnesses testifying at a hearing before the Board shall be required to take an oath or affirmation before testifying. Any member of the Board may administer oaths and affirmations, ask questions of any witness, and each party shall have the opportunity to ask questions of each witness and the other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board shall manage the conduct of the hearing and may limit the number of witnesses or scope of questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits in hearing — submission and marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specifically excluded, all documents submitted by the parties through their statements under §222.15 shall be deemed admitted and marked as exhibits in the same order as presented through the documentary evidence a party submitted with the party statement. Additional documents allowed at hearing may be presented as exhibits and marked by the presenting party starting with the next number after the exhibits attached to the party's document statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should attach documentary evidence to the party statement to ensure admission and proper exhibit numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary exhibits requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents of voluminous documentary evidence which cannot be conveniently examined at the hearing may be presented in the form of a chart, summary, or calculation. Absent leave of the Board, evidence supporting the summary exhibit must have been produced to the other parties in discovery and admitted as exhibits, and the summary exhibit must be disclosed to the other parties in the proceeding at least seven days before the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for summary exhibits must be in the record and disclosed in advance; seek leave if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: New exhibits for cross/redirect require leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits not submitted as part of written testimony may not be used at a hearing without leave of the Board. Leave to use such exhibits may be requested before or during the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to use such exhibits follow §220.5(a)(1). Untimely or unauthorized use may be barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for unsuitability — Board process and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board determines that a claim or counterclaim should be dismissed for unsuitability under 17 U.S.C. 1506(f)(3), the Board shall issue an order stating its intention to dismiss the claim without prejudice and allow the claimant or counterclaimant 30 days to request reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following the response period, the Board will render its final decision; procedural limits for requests are set out in §220.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration request limits for unsuitability dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days following issuance of an order, the claimant or counterclaimant may request that the Board reconsider its determination of unsuitability. If the proceeding is active, the respondent may file a response within 30 days. A request or response shall not exceed 7 pages and shall meet the requirements of §220.5(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict page limits and procedural form requirements apply to such requests and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party-initiated request to dismiss for unsuitability
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time, any party who believes that a claim or counterclaim is unsuitable for determination by the Board may file a request that shall not exceed five pages providing the basis for such belief. An opposing party may file a response within 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests and responses must meet §220.5(a)(2) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard discovery practice and use of standard forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, discovery in proceedings before the Board shall be limited to the methods set forth in this part and shall use the standard forms provided on the Board's website. Discovery responses and documents shall be served on the other parties and shall not be filed with the Board unless as part of written testimony or as needed in support of other filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Board-provided standard interrogatory and document-request forms; do not file routine discovery with the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications for discovery materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All discovery material exchanged among the parties must include a certification. For interrogatory or requests for admission responses, the certification shall affirm that the responses are accurate and truthful to the best of the submitting party's knowledge. For production of documents, the certification shall affirm that the produced documents are genuine and unaltered to the best of the producing party's knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications are required on all discovery responses and productions to attest to accuracy and authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable investigation duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall make a reasonable investigation under the circumstances to adequately respond to discovery requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses that assert lack of knowledge must state that reasonable investigation was made and that available information is insufficient to admit or deny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of discovery per scheduling order
rubrics_metrics.description: The exchange of discovery material shall take place at the times and within the deadlines specified by the scheduling order. The Board may modify deadlines upon a showing of good cause or on its own initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for modification follow §220.5(a)(1); parties may make oral or written requests during conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-discovery conferences and virtual format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall hold a pre-discovery conference and a post-discovery conference. The Board may hold additional conferences to manage discovery and resolve disputes; conferences shall be held virtually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferences may be held by one or more Copyright Claims Officers and procedural requests tied to conferences follow §220.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad definition of 'document' for discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'document' includes writings, drawings, graphs, charts, photographs, sound recordings, images, and other data or data compilations stored in any medium from which information can be obtained directly or after translation into a reasonably usable form, whether in written or electronic form, an object, or otherwise. The Board shall read this definition broadly to ensure comprehensive production so long as that production can be easily accomplished by a layperson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect wide-ranging categories of materials to be discoverable; the Board limits requests to what is reasonably producible by a layperson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard interrogatories — general content
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties in an active proceeding shall use the set of standard interrogatories provided on the Board's website, which shall consist of information pertaining to: (1) identity of witnesses and subject matter, (2) identity of other individuals with material information, (3) any agreement or relationship between parties relevant to the claim, (4) any harm or damages sought, and (5) materially responsive documents the party is aware exist or once existed but are not in its possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard interrogatory forms and provide complete information in these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard interrogatories — asserting infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional interrogatories for a party asserting infringement include: (1) copyright registration details, (2) compliance with copyright formalities, (3) ownership of the copyright, (4) publication, (5) creation date and process and joint/derivative/work-for-hire issues, (6) preexisting elements for derivative works and related ownership/rights, (7) basis for belief the alleged infringer gained access, (8) basis for belief activities constitute infringement, (9) discovery of the alleged infringement, (10) description and calculation of damages, and (11) attempts to stop or mitigate infringement prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed factual and documentary support for each item; these interrogatories flesh out core infringement elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard interrogatories — non-infringement response
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional interrogatories for a party asserting non-infringement include: (1) ownership of the allegedly infringing material, (2) dissemination history of the material, (3) creation date/process and joint/derivative/work-for-hire issues, (4) preexisting elements and ownership/rights for derivative works, (5) any information indicating the claimant does not own a copyright in the allegedly infringed work, (6) all defenses to infringement with detailed basis, (7) basis for belief actions do not constitute infringement, (8) continued use or dissemination of the material, and (9) revenues/profits and deductible expenses related to the sale/use of the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defenses listed in timely answers and updated answers will be considered by the Board without requiring claim amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard interrogatories — misrepresentation claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims under 17 U.S.C. 512(f), interrogatories shall include: (1) the notification or counter-notification at issue, (2) identity of the ISP to which it was sent, (3) communications with ISP/parties related to the notice, (4) basis for belief the notice included a misrepresentation, and (5) harm including description and calculation of damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide communications and documentary evidence supporting misrepresentation and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to update interrogatory responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A party has an obligation to update its interrogatory responses and serve updated responses on the other parties as soon as practicable after the discovery of new or updated information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing duty to supplement responses when new information is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard requests for production — general content
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall use the Board's standard requests for production, which shall include copies of: (1) all documents the party is likely to use in support of its claims or defenses, (2) all other documents reasonably known that conflict with the party's claims or defenses, and (3) all documents referred to in, or used in preparing, responses to standard interrogatories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce relevant supportive and adverse documents; standard forms provided on Board website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard requests for production — asserting infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement-related production requests include: (1) the work claimed to be infringed, its copyright registration, and correspondence with the Copyright Office, (2) the allegedly infringing material if reasonably available, (3) documents showing preexisting works used for derivative works and ownership/rights, (4) documents related to the allegedly infringing material including communications, (5) documents showing or negating ownership or rights (agreements), (6) documents sufficient to show damages, and (7) documents showing attempts to stop or mitigate infringement prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registration and ownership proof, derivation evidence, and damage substantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document searches and ESI proportionality limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall conduct a reasonable search for responsive documents of any files in its possession or control, including agents' files. ESI responsive to requests should be searched, but ESI searches need not exceed manual searches that are easily accomplished by a layperson and parties need not conduct searches that would reasonably require assistance of third parties (e.g., document vendors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation extends to agents/employees, but not to burdensome vendor-assisted collection; tailor ESI searches to what a layperson can accomplish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluminous/irrelevant productions prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to document requests that include large amounts of irrelevant or duplicative material are prohibited and may constitute bad-faith conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overproduction of irrelevant materials; produce only responsive, non-duplicative documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to update productions and preserve documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A party has an obligation to preserve all material documents and to update its production of documents by providing to the other parties any documents it later finds responsive to the Board's standard requests or other allowed requests as soon as practicable after discovery of such documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing preservation and supplementation obligations; late-found documents must be produced promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileged documents and procedure to withhold
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential communications with external counsel or in-house counsel reflecting or seeking legal advice related to the merits of the proceeding shall be considered privileged and need not be produced or logged. Parties must seek leave of the Board to withhold additional documents as privileged by filing a request with the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File privilege requests following §220.5(a)(1); otherwise, privileged materials must be identified and leave sought to withhold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional discovery standard — narrow tailoring and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional discovery requested must be narrowly tailored to the issues at hand, not covered by the standard discovery, highly likely to lead to production of information relevant to the core issues, and not result in an undue burden on the responding party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that are broad or marginally relevant will be disfavored; show specificity and direct link to core issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting additional discovery — good cause and balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will grant a request for additional discovery upon a showing of good cause. In considering such a request, the Board shall balance the needs and circumstances of the case against the burden on any party, along with the amount in dispute and the overall goal of efficient resolution of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why standard discovery is insufficient and demonstrate proportionality and efficiency considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for additional discovery requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for additional discovery must specifically indicate the type of additional discovery requested and the information sought (including the specific requests themselves), set forth in detail the need for the request, and indicate whether the other parties consent or object to the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural format of §220.5(a)(2) for filing requests and responses; include explanations and attachments as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert witnesses disfavored; exceptional circumstances only
rubrics_metrics.description: An expert witness may be used only with leave of the Board. The use of expert witnesses is highly disfavored and requests shall be rarely granted; the Board will permit an expert only in exceptional circumstances upon a showing the case cannot fairly proceed without the expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board balances need, burden, costs, rebuttal burdens, amount in dispute, and efficient resolution when deciding expert requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and contents of expert witness request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an expert must indicate the topics of proposed testimony, the name of the proposed expert, the anticipated cost of retaining the expert, set forth the basis and justifications for the request, and indicate whether the other parties consent or object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests follow §220.5(a)(2) procedures and should include cost and justification details to show necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of expert testimony if permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Any permitted expert testimony must be submitted as an expert statement that is sworn under penalty of perjury, organized into numbered paragraphs, detailed as to the substance of the expert's opinion and the basis therefor, disclose facts or data considered, describe the expert's qualifications including publications and speaking engagements in the previous 10 years, list all other cases in which the expert testified in the previous four years, and include a statement of compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict content and formatting requirements; failure to comply may lead to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized expert testimony excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Any expert testimony that is introduced in any way without the Board's express permission shall be stricken by the Board and shall not be considered in the Board's determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to introduce expert evidence without Board leave; it will be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for admission — disfavored and form rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for admission may be served only with leave of the Board and are disfavored. They may pertain to facts, application of law to fact, opinions, or genuineness of documents (a copy must be attached). Each matter must be separately stated in a numbered paragraph; compound requests are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek Board leave and follow strict single-issue numbering; attach copies for document genuineness requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses to requests for admission — specificity and investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: A response must be served by the time specified. A matter admitted is conclusively established unless the Board permits withdrawal for good cause. If not admitted, the answer must specifically deny it or state in detail why the responding party cannot truthfully admit or deny. Lack of knowledge may be asserted only if the party states it has made reasonable investigation and that available information is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must fairly respond to substance; partial admissions must specify which part is admitted and which denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to requests for admission — Board discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: A matter is not automatically admitted if a party fails to respond within the required timeframe. However, the Board may deem it admitted in its discretion subject to application of adverse inferences under 17 U.S.C. 1506(n)(3) per §225.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-response is risky; the Board may apply adverse consequences or deem admissions in discovery sanctions contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositions shall not be permitted in proceedings before the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not seek or attempt to take depositions; discovery tools are limited to interrogatories, document requests, requests for admission (with leave), and limited additional discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to attempt informal resolution of discovery disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve any discovery disputes without the involvement of the Board. A party must confer with an opposing party in an attempt to reach a resolution prior to raising any discovery dispute with the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document efforts to confer and resolve disputes before filing; failure to attempt may affect dispute resolution outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for conference to resolve discovery dispute — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: If attempts fail, the party seeking discovery may file a request for a conference that shall: describe the dispute, state that party's position, explain attempts made to resolve the dispute without Board involvement, and attach any inadequate interrogatory responses or inadequate request-for-admission responses. Requests follow §220.5(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include supporting communications and specific examples of deficiencies to aid Board review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board resolution of discovery disputes and compliance deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving a request and any response, the Board may schedule a conference and shall issue an order resolving the dispute and, if in favor of the aggrieved party, set a deadline for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply promptly with Board orders or risk sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to comply with discovery order and notice period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party fails to timely comply with the Board's discovery order, the seeking party may send a notice giving the noncompliant party 10 days to comply. If noncompliance continues after 10 days, the aggrieved party may file a request for sanctions with the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the 10-day cure period before filing for sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions — form, standard for granting, and relief
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for sanctions shall be uploaded to eCCB and meet §220.5(a)(2) requirements, attach relevant inadequate discovery responses (except for document-request disputes), and set forth the basis. The Board may hold a conference and, in its sole discretion and upon good cause shown, impose sanctions. Sanctions may include an adverse inference with respect to disputed facts and may be considered when awarding attorneys' fees and costs during a final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidentiary support for sanctions requests; sanctions are discretionary and require showing of noncompliance and good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for smaller claims proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When total monetary relief sought in a claim does not exceed $5,000 (exclusive of attorneys' fees and costs), the claimant may choose to have the proceeding adjudicated under the smaller-claims procedures in this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claimant may elect smaller claims at filing and generally follow the streamlined Part 226 procedures; other specified CFR parts also apply as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and amendment of smaller-claims election
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimant may request consideration under the smaller-claims procedures at the time of filing and may change its choice at any time before service of the initial notice. If the initial notice has been issued, the claimant must request reissuance to change the choice. Once the claimant has served the initial notice on any respondent, the claimant may not amend its choice without consent of the other parties and leave of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election timing matters—once initial notice is served, changing the election requires consent and Board leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of counterclaims in smaller-claims proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claimant has chosen smaller-claims procedures, a respondent may assert a counterclaim only if it seeks total monetary relief of $5,000 or less (exclusive of attorneys' fees or costs). Any permissible counterclaims shall be adjudicated under the procedures set forth in this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterclaims exceeding the monetary cap are not permitted in smaller-claims proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller claims — single Officer hearing and rotating assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: A smaller claims proceeding shall be heard by one Copyright Claims Officer. One of the three Officers shall hear smaller claims proceedings on a rotating basis at the Board's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are decided by a single Officer to streamline process; scheduling follows Part 226 rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller-claims initial conference and limited discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial conference will replace the pre-discovery conference. The presiding Officer shall explain steps of proceeding and discuss nature of claims, counterclaims, defenses, and possibility of settlement. During the initial conference, the presiding Officer shall discuss whether additional documents/information beyond materials attached to claim and response are necessary; any order for production shall be narrowly tailored to the merits and highly likely to lead to relevant information without undue burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery in smaller claims is tightly limited and ordered only when narrowly necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits conference submissions in smaller claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 14 days before the merits conference, each party shall file with the presiding Officer evidence it wishes to be considered and any evidence requested by the Officer. All such evidence must have been served on the other parties before filing unless received from the other side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may also submit a written statement (limited to seven pages per §220.5(b)) setting forth positions, defenses, counterclaims, and damages sought.
